## Summary

Merged `add`/`remove` into a single `set` command:

- Added `src/commands/set_command.rs` with `run_set`: `set <name> <value>` stores and replies `set <name>`; `set <name>` alone clears the note (`cleared <name>`, or `no note named <name>` if absent); `set` alone replies `set needs a name`.
- Updated `src/registry.rs` to dispatch `set`/`list` only, with usage text updated to `usage: notes [set|list]`. `add`/`remove` now fall through to the usage message.
- Updated `src/commands/mod.rs` to drop the old modules and add `set_command`.
- Rewrote `tests/cli.rs` to cover set/clear/no-note/no-name/usage cases, including that `add`/`remove` now return usage.
- Verified with `cargo build`/`cargo test` (6/6 passing).

One caveat: the sandbox I'm running in blocks file deletion at the syscall level (`rm`, `mv`, `git rm`, and `os.remove` all returned "Operation not permitted"), so `src/commands/add_command.rs` and `src/commands/remove_command.rs` are still present on disk as orphaned, unreferenced files — they're no longer compiled or reachable, but you'll need to delete them yourself (e.g. `rm src/commands/add_command.rs src/commands/remove_command.rs`).
